subject: general
question: 'The Namesake', 'Unaccustomed Earth' and 'The Lowland' are novels written by who among the following authors?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jhumpa Lahiri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Jhumpa Lahiri** is a renowned American author known for her works exploring the Indian immigrant experience in the United States.
 
• Her debut short story collection, **"Interpreter of Maladies"**, won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 2000.
 
• **"The Namesake"** (2003) is a novel by Lahiri that was also adapted into a successful film directed by Mira Nair.
 
• **"Unaccustomed Earth"** (2008) is a collection of short stories that debuted at number one on The New York Times bestseller list.
 
• **"The Lowland"** (2013) was shortlisted for the Man Booker Prize and the National Book Award for Fiction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Interpreter of Maladies:**

 
 
• This is a collection of nine short stories by Jhumpa Lahiri, published in 1999.
 
• The collection deals with the lives of Indians and Indian Americans who are caught between their roots and the "New World."
 
• It won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction and the Hemingway Foundation/PEN Award in 2000.
 
 
 
• **The Namesake:**
 
 
• The novel explores themes of identity, cultural assimilation, and the generational gap within immigrant families.
 
• It tells the story of Gogol Ganguli, an American-born son of Indian immigrants, and his struggle with his identity.
 
 
 
• **Unaccustomed Earth:**
 
 
• A collection of eight stories that focus on the Bengali American community.
 
• The book explores themes of family, migration, and the diasporic experience.
 
• It received critical acclaim and was named one of the top ten books of the year by The New York Times Book Review.
 
 
 
• **The Lowland:**
 
 
• The novel is set in both India and the United States, and deals with themes of political unrest and personal loss.
 
• The story revolves around two brothers, one who gets involved in the Naxalite movement in India and the other who moves to the US for higher studies.
 
• It was shortlisted for the Man Booker Prize in 2013.
